reuse.why: Builds applyWeekendRule on the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend, recurConfigToRSchedule, RSchedule and monthUtils, and every weekend site (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, schedule-template, the new getDatesInRange) calls it.

duplication.why: The three inline skipWeekend ternaries are replaced by one definition; what remains repeated is the occurrence-to-day mapping and the over-fetch/filter loops in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: The rule and holiday helpers live in shared/schedules.ts next to getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the new handler sits with getUpcomingDates in schedules/app.ts; the rrule data shape is aligned in rule-utils.

scope.why: Edits serve the steps; renaming weekendSolve to weekendSolveMode in the rrule data is a small incidental alignment that widens the change.

maintainability.why: A future weekend change is made in applyWeekendRule, though magic over-fetch counts (take: 7, count * 7) and the getMaxWeekendShiftDays bound couple callers to the rule's internals.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All weekend decisions go through applyWeekendRule; getNextDate's pre-existing noSkipWeekend option is the only local branch.

disguised_duplication.where: The occurrence-window/filter code in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange is similar but open, not disguised copying of a shared definition.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts: applyWeekendRule's rule object gains frequency and holidays and getDateWithSkippedWeekend a holidays parameter; one daily-skip branch inside applyWeekendRule; all callers route through it, so growth follows the requirements rather than drifting.
